description: MySQL 8.4 LTS health metric catalog. Derived from dbi services scoring framework. Technology-specific implementation of the universal pillar/subcategory structure. Metric semantics validated against MySQL 8.4 LTS and 9.x innovation releases.
release_notes: v1.3.1 (2026-09-23): catalog maturity label added (draft: not yet reviewed by a technology leader, neither for collection nor for scoring). No metric, threshold, weight or rule change. v1.3.0 (PoC): seven hot metrics refactored to use scoring-core v1.5.0 profile-keyed thresholds, plus two long-flagged placement moves applied (mirror of MariaDB v1.3.0 PoC). Affected metrics: CAP-3.2 (purge_lag profile-keyed), PERF-3.1 (innodb_row_lock_waits profile-keyed), PERF-1.1 (buffer_pool_hit_ratio profile-keyed), CAP-3.1 (innodb_buffer_pool_hit_rate MOVED to perf_cache + profile-keyed), CAP-2.2 (thread_cache_hit_rate MOVED to perf_cache), PERF-2.6 (full_table_scan_rate profile-keyed), PERF-3.3 (metadata_lock_waits profile-keyed). All patches compatible with MySQL 8.4 LTS and 9.x. v1.2.0: schema-ready for consistency_rules (rules deferred to Technology Leader work). v1.1.0: Subcategory point allocations within Capacity, Performance, and Future-Proofing pillars differ from the architecture specification (SCORING_SYSTEM_ARCHITECTURE.md section 2.3). These splits have been stable since v1.0.0 and are flagged for tech-leader review. See docs/guides/metric-placement-review.md for details.

metrics.description: Whether the MySQL binary log (log_bin) is on. Required for point-in-time recovery and replication.
metrics.remediation: Enable binary logging: log_bin = /var/lib/mysql/mysql-bin in my.cnf

metrics.description: Binary log format (binlog_format). ROW is required for reliable replication and PITR; STATEMENT/MIXED can produce non-deterministic results.
metrics.remediation: Set binlog_format = ROW in my.cnf for reliable replication and PITR

metrics.description: Binary log retention window (binlog_expire_logs_seconds). Must cover the PITR recovery window (target 1-30 days).
metrics.remediation: Set binlog_expire_logs_seconds (MySQL 8.0+) or expire_logs_days in my.cnf

metrics.description: Whether Global Transaction IDs (gtid_mode) are on. Required for reliable replication failover and PITR.
metrics.remediation: Enable GTID: gtid_mode = ON and enforce_gtid_consistency = ON in my.cnf

metrics.description: Whether the binary log is flushed per transaction (sync_binlog=1). Required to avoid losing committed transactions on crash.
metrics.remediation: Set sync_binlog = 1 in my.cnf for crash-safe binary logging

metrics.description: Whether a regular backup schedule is defined and running. Required to bound the data loss window.
metrics.remediation: Document and implement a backup schedule (daily recommended)

metrics.description: Age of the most recent successful backup. Must stay within the RPO window or recovery loses data beyond policy.
metrics.remediation: Verify backup jobs are running and completing successfully

metrics.description: Whether a logical backup (mysqldump or mysqlpump) is scheduled alongside physical backups. Useful for selective restore and version migrations.
metrics.remediation: Schedule regular mysqldump for logical backup in addition to physical backups

metrics.description: Whether backups are periodically verified for integrity. Untested backups cannot be relied on for actual recovery.
metrics.remediation: Implement backup verification process (restore tests on non-production)

metrics.description: Backup tool in use. Enterprise tools (MySQL Enterprise Backup, Percona XtraBackup) provide hot, consistent physical backups with minimal locking.
metrics.remediation: Consider implementing Percona XtraBackup for hot physical backups

metrics.description: Whether point-in-time recovery via binary logs is available. Without it, recovery is limited to the last full backup.
metrics.remediation: Enable binary logging and test PITR procedures using mysqlbinlog

metrics.description: Whether backups are encrypted at rest. Required to protect backup files from offline disclosure if storage is compromised.
metrics.remediation: Enable backup encryption using MySQL Enterprise Backup or XtraBackup --encrypt

metrics.description: Whether a replica (ideally a delayed replica) is available as a DR target. Required for fast failover and protection against logical corruption.
metrics.remediation: Configure a delayed replica (CHANGE REPLICATION SOURCE ... DELAY = N) for DR

metrics.description: Whether a Recovery Point Objective is documented. Required to size backup frequency and binlog retention against allowed data loss.
metrics.remediation: Define and document RPO target based on business requirements

metrics.description: Whether a Recovery Time Objective is documented. Required to choose a recovery strategy that meets allowed downtime.
metrics.remediation: Define and document RTO target based on business requirements

metrics.description: Whether a restore drill has been performed in the last 90 days. Untested restores routinely surface broken procedures during real incidents.
metrics.remediation: Schedule regular restore tests (at least quarterly)

metrics.description: Whether a disaster recovery plan exists. Required to coordinate response under time pressure when systems are down.
metrics.remediation: Document disaster recovery procedures and runbooks

metrics.description: Whether backup retention covers the organisation's policy window (regulatory, compliance, business). Insufficient retention violates policy.
metrics.remediation: Configure backup retention to meet compliance requirements

metrics.description: Whether binary log retention covers the PITR window. Insufficient retention shrinks the recoverable timeframe.
metrics.remediation: Ensure binlog retention covers required recovery window (binlog_expire_logs_seconds)

metrics.description: Whether backups are replicated to offsite or separate storage. Required so a primary-site failure does not destroy all recovery copies.
metrics.remediation: Implement offsite backup copies to S3, Azure Blob, or remote storage

metrics.description: Share of client connections using TLS. Must be 100% to prevent in-clear credentials and query traffic on the wire.
metrics.remediation: Set require_secure_transport = ON and configure clients to use TLS

metrics.description: Default authentication plugin (default_authentication_plugin). Required to be a strong algorithm (caching_sha2_password or ed25519); legacy mysql_native_password is weak.
metrics.remediation: Set default_authentication_plugin = caching_sha2_password in my.cnf

metrics.description: Password policy enforcement via validate_password. Required to prevent weak passwords; must be at MEDIUM or STRONG.
metrics.remediation: Install validate_password component: INSTALL COMPONENT 'file://component_validate_password'

metrics.description: Failed login attempts in the last 24h. Spikes can indicate brute-force attempts or misconfigured clients.
metrics.remediation: Investigate failed login sources and implement connection_control plugin

metrics.description: Default password lifetime (default_password_lifetime). Required to enforce periodic password rotation per policy.
metrics.remediation: Set default_password_lifetime = 90 in my.cnf

metrics.description: Whether TLS is enforced for all client connections (require_secure_transport). Without it, plaintext connections are accepted.
metrics.remediation: Set require_secure_transport = ON in my.cnf

metrics.description: Minimum accepted TLS version (tls_version). Must be 1.2 or higher; older protocols are deprecated and have known vulnerabilities.
metrics.remediation: Set tls_version = 'TLSv1.2,TLSv1.3' in my.cnf

metrics.description: Whether InnoDB tablespace encryption (TDE) is on. Required to protect data files at rest from offline disclosure.
metrics.remediation: Enable InnoDB tablespace encryption: default_table_encryption = ON, configure keyring plugin

metrics.description: Whether binary log files are encrypted at rest (binlog_encryption). Required to keep replicated changes confidential on disk.
metrics.remediation: Enable binary log encryption: binlog_encryption = ON in my.cnf

metrics.description: Days remaining before the SSL certificate expires. Must stay above 30 days to leave room for renewal before client breakage.
metrics.remediation: Renew SSL certificate before expiration (check ssl_ca, ssl_cert system variables)

metrics.description: Whether an audit plugin (MySQL Enterprise Audit or community equivalent) is loaded. Required for compliance audit trails.
metrics.remediation: Install audit plugin: INSTALL PLUGIN audit_log SONAME 'audit_log.so'

metrics.description: Whether the slow query log is on. Required for performance analysis and detecting unusual query patterns.
metrics.remediation: Set slow_query_log = ON and long_query_time in my.cnf

metrics.description: Whether the error log writes to a persistent file (log_error). Required to retain post-mortem evidence beyond the running session.
metrics.remediation: Set log_error to a persistent file path in my.cnf

metrics.description: Whether --log-raw is off. When on, passwords appear in cleartext in the general query log — a serious security risk.
metrics.remediation: Ensure --log-raw is NOT set in my.cnf (it logs passwords in cleartext)

metrics.description: Log retention duration. Must cover the compliance/forensic window (typically 90+ days) so post-incident analysis is possible.
metrics.remediation: Configure log rotation to retain logs for compliance period

metrics.description: Whether root accounts are restricted to localhost. Remote root access vastly enlarges the brute-force / lateral-movement surface.
metrics.remediation: DELETE FROM mysql.user WHERE User='root' AND Host NOT IN ('localhost','127.0.0.1','::1')

metrics.description: Number of accounts holding the SUPER privilege. Must be kept minimal; SUPER bypasses many access controls.
metrics.remediation: Revoke SUPER from unnecessary accounts; use granular privileges instead

metrics.description: Number of anonymous (empty-username) accounts. Any are unsafe — they let unauthenticated clients connect.
metrics.remediation: DROP USER ''@'localhost'; DROP USER ''@'%';

metrics.description: Accounts with wildcard '%' host and broad privileges. Must be eliminated; wildcard hosts allow connections from any source IP.
metrics.remediation: Restrict user accounts to specific hosts rather than '%' wildcard

metrics.description: Number of accounts holding GRANT OPTION. Must be kept minimal; the privilege lets a user delegate any of its rights to others.
metrics.remediation: Revoke GRANT OPTION from accounts that do not need to delegate privileges

metrics.description: Data directory disk usage. Must stay under 85%; a full data volume halts MySQL writes.
metrics.remediation: Add disk capacity or archive/purge old data

metrics.description: Projected days until InnoDB shared tablespace or data files fill the volume. Short horizons require capacity planning.
metrics.remediation: Plan capacity expansion or implement data lifecycle management

metrics.description: Free-space ratio inside table files (fragmentation). High values waste storage and slow scans; OPTIMIZE TABLE reclaims space.
metrics.remediation: Run OPTIMIZE TABLE or ALTER TABLE ... ENGINE=InnoDB to reclaim space

metrics.description: InnoDB redo log capacity (innodb_log_file_size or innodb_redo_log_capacity). Must be sized for write throughput to avoid checkpoint stalls.
metrics.remediation: Tune innodb_log_file_size (or innodb_redo_log_capacity in MySQL 8.0.30+)

metrics.description: Whether data directory size is being tracked. Required as input to capacity planning and growth forecasting.
metrics.remediation: Configure monitoring for MySQL data directory size growth

metrics.description: Active connections vs max_connections. Sustained use above 80% leaves no headroom for spikes and risks 'too many connections' errors.
metrics.remediation: Increase max_connections or implement connection pooling (ProxySQL)

metrics.description: Thread cache effectiveness (Threads_created vs Connections). Low hit rates indicate frequent thread creation overhead — a performance / caching concern. Moved from capacity_connections in v1.3.0 per docs/guides/metric-placement-review.md §2A.
metrics.remediation: Increase thread_cache_size to reduce thread creation overhead

metrics.description: Whether a connection pooler (ProxySQL or MySQL Router) is in front of the server. Required to absorb spikes and amortise connection cost.
metrics.remediation: Implement ProxySQL for connection pooling and query routing

metrics.description: Share of aborted connections vs total. Sustained values above 1% indicate timeouts, oversized packets, or auth issues.
metrics.remediation: Investigate aborted connections: check max_allowed_packet, wait_timeout, net_read_timeout

metrics.description: Headroom between peak connections (Max_used_connections) and max_connections. Must keep at least 20% spare to absorb spikes.
metrics.remediation: Review Max_used_connections vs max_connections; resize or implement pooling

metrics.display_name: InnoDB Buffer Pool Hit Ratio Healthy
metrics.description: InnoDB buffer pool hit ratio. Low values force disk reads and degrade query latency; healthy values depend on workload type — OLTP workloads should sit near 99%, OLAP workloads with working sets larger than RAM operate healthily lower. Moved from capacity_maintenance in v1.3.0 per docs/guides/metric-placement-review.md §2A.
metrics.remediation: Increase innodb_buffer_pool_size (target 70-80% of available RAM)

metrics.description: InnoDB undo history list length (purge lag, in rows). Sustained high values indicate long-running transactions blocking purge and bloating undo; write-heavy OLTP workloads naturally accumulate more undo than read-heavy or analytical workloads.
metrics.remediation: Investigate long-running transactions causing purge lag; check innodb_max_purge_lag

metrics.description: Tables with high free-space fragmentation (>30%). High counts indicate OPTIMIZE TABLE is overdue and disk usage is inflated.
metrics.remediation: Run OPTIMIZE TABLE for heavily fragmented tables during maintenance window

metrics.description: Whether table statistics are recent. Stale stats lead the optimizer to choose poor execution plans.
metrics.remediation: Run ANALYZE TABLE on tables with stale statistics; enable innodb_stats_auto_recalc

metrics.description: Whether the event_scheduler is on. Required if maintenance events (scheduled cleanup, stats refresh) are defined in the database.
metrics.remediation: Set event_scheduler = ON if using MySQL events for maintenance tasks

metrics.description: Buffer pool partitioning (innodb_buffer_pool_instances). Must be sized to pool capacity to reduce contention; rule of thumb 1 per GB up to 8-16.
metrics.remediation: Set innodb_buffer_pool_instances = 1 per GB of buffer pool (max 8-16)

metrics.description: Headroom on AUTO_INCREMENT columns vs the column's max value. Approaching the limit risks INSERT failures with no headroom left.
metrics.remediation: Alter column to BIGINT UNSIGNED before reaching INT/BIGINT limit

metrics.description: Projected days until the data volume fills based on growth trend. Must stay above 180 days to leave time for capacity expansion.
metrics.remediation: Plan storage expansion or data archival strategy

metrics.description: Whether capacity reviews happen at least quarterly. Required to catch growth trends before they cause incidents.
metrics.remediation: Establish a regular capacity review process

metrics.description: Whether very large tables use partitioning. Partitioning helps with maintenance windows, archival, and query pruning on huge datasets.
metrics.remediation: Consider partitioning tables exceeding 100M rows for easier maintenance

metrics.display_name: Buffer Pool Read Hit Rate Healthy
metrics.description: InnoDB buffer pool read hit rate. Low rates push load to disk; healthy values depend on workload type — OLTP workloads should sit near 99%, OLAP workloads with working sets larger than RAM operate healthily lower.
metrics.remediation: Increase innodb_buffer_pool_size; target 70-80% of total RAM

metrics.description: Whether the legacy query cache is still in use. The query cache is removed in MySQL 8.0; keeping it on a 5.7 server hurts scalability.
metrics.remediation: Query cache was removed in MySQL 8.0; use ProxySQL or application-level caching

metrics.description: MyISAM key cache size (key_buffer_size). On InnoDB-only deployments it should be kept minimal so RAM goes to the buffer pool instead.
metrics.remediation: Reduce key_buffer_size to ~8M if not using MyISAM tables

metrics.description: Table open cache hit ratio. Should stay above 90%; below that, table_open_cache likely needs to grow.
metrics.remediation: Increase table_open_cache if Opened_tables/Uptime ratio is high

metrics.description: Per-session sort buffer size (sort_buffer_size). Should sit in the 256K-4M range; oversized values inflate per-connection memory.
metrics.remediation: Tune sort_buffer_size based on workload; avoid setting too large (per-session allocation)

metrics.description: Whether performance_schema is on. Required for query analysis, slow-query attribution, and most observability tooling.
metrics.remediation: Set performance_schema = ON in my.cnf

metrics.description: Whether the slow query log is on. Required to identify problematic queries beyond a configured duration threshold.
metrics.remediation: Set slow_query_log = ON in my.cnf

metrics.description: Slow query duration threshold (long_query_time). A value of 1 second or less is required to capture slow queries effectively.
metrics.remediation: Set long_query_time = 1 (or lower) in my.cnf to capture slow queries

metrics.description: Whether queries without indexes are logged (log_queries_not_using_indexes). Required to catch full-scan regressions.
metrics.remediation: Set log_queries_not_using_indexes = ON in my.cnf

metrics.description: Whether top-cost queries from Performance Schema are reviewed periodically. Required to keep optimisation effort focused on real workload.
metrics.remediation: Review performance_schema.events_statements_summary_by_digest regularly

metrics.description: Share of queries doing full table scans. Sustained high rates indicate missing indexes or non-sargable predicates; analytical (OLAP) workloads naturally generate more scans than OLTP, where indexes should cover most access patterns.
metrics.remediation: Add indexes to eliminate full table scans; use EXPLAIN to identify queries

metrics.description: Rate of disk-spilled filesorts (Sort_merge_passes). High rates indicate ORDER BY/GROUP BY without supporting indexes or undersized sort_buffer_size.
metrics.remediation: Add indexes to ORDER BY / GROUP BY columns; increase sort_buffer_size

metrics.description: InnoDB row-lock wait count. Sustained high counts indicate transaction contention; write-heavy OLTP workloads tolerate more row-lock waits than read-heavy or analytical workloads.
metrics.remediation: Investigate blocking queries via performance_schema.data_locks; optimize transactions

metrics.description: InnoDB deadlock count. Sustained deadlocks indicate inconsistent transaction order or hot-row contention in the application.
metrics.remediation: Enable innodb_print_all_deadlocks = ON; review application transaction order

metrics.description: Metadata-lock waits affecting DDL. Sustained waits mean schema changes are blocked behind long-running transactions; high-concurrency OLTP environments should tolerate near-zero waits because a single waiting DDL stalls all dependent sessions.
metrics.remediation: Check performance_schema.metadata_locks; ensure DDLs run when no long transactions are open

metrics.description: Share of statements waiting on table-level locks. Sustained values above 5% point to MyISAM tables or coarse-locking patterns.
metrics.remediation: Migrate MyISAM tables to InnoDB; InnoDB uses row-level locking

metrics.description: Replica lag (Seconds_Behind_Source). Must stay under 30 seconds for read scaling and timely failover; sustained lag widens the data loss window.
metrics.remediation: Investigate replica SQL thread lag; consider parallel replication (replica_parallel_workers)

metrics.description: Whether the replica SQL thread is applying events. If stopped, replication has stalled and the replica falls behind the source.
metrics.remediation: Check SHOW REPLICA STATUS; investigate and restart replica SQL thread

metrics.description: Whether the replica IO thread is connected to the source and pulling binlog events. If stopped, no new events reach the replica.
metrics.remediation: Check network connectivity to source; review replica error log

metrics.description: Whether the replica has only GTIDs originating from the source. Errant transactions on the replica break safe failover.
metrics.remediation: Investigate errant transactions using GTID_SUBTRACT(); use pt-table-checksum

metrics.description: Whether the MySQL/MariaDB server version was successfully read. Required as the input for EOL and minor-version checks.
metrics.remediation: Upgrade to MySQL 8.4 LTS (current LTS) or MySQL 9.x (Innovation)

metrics.description: Whether the server is on the latest minor/patch release within its major version. Falling behind misses bug and security fixes.
metrics.remediation: Apply latest MySQL patch release for bug fixes and security patches

metrics.description: Whether the running MySQL/MariaDB version is still under vendor support. EOL versions no longer receive security patches.
metrics.remediation: Upgrade from EOL MySQL version; consult Oracle MySQL lifecycle page

metrics.description: Tables on engines other than InnoDB. MyISAM/MEMORY lack crash recovery and row-level locking and should not hold persistent data.
metrics.remediation: Convert MyISAM tables to InnoDB: ALTER TABLE t ENGINE = InnoDB

metrics.description: Whether the server is on the LTS release track (8.4.x or next LTS). LTS gets longer support and fewer breaking changes than Innovation.
metrics.remediation: Consider MySQL 8.4 LTS over Innovation releases for production stability

metrics.description: Whether a high-availability solution (InnoDB Cluster, Group Replication, or ProxySQL+replication) is in use. Required to survive node failures without downtime.
metrics.remediation: Implement InnoDB Cluster or Group Replication for automatic failover

metrics.description: Whether ProxySQL or MySQL Router fronts the cluster. Required for transparent failover and read/write split without app-side wiring.
metrics.remediation: Deploy ProxySQL for connection pooling, query routing, and failover transparency

metrics.description: Whether innodb_strict_mode is on. Required to surface invalid CREATE/ALTER options as errors instead of silent truncation.
metrics.remediation: Set innodb_strict_mode = ON in my.cnf

metrics.description: Whether a database version upgrade plan exists. Required to keep ahead of EOL and avoid emergency upgrades under pressure.
metrics.remediation: Document upgrade path and schedule before current version approaches EOL

metrics.description: Accounts using the deprecated mysql_native_password plugin. Must be migrated to caching_sha2_password for forward compatibility.
metrics.remediation: Migrate accounts to caching_sha2_password: ALTER USER x IDENTIFIED WITH caching_sha2_password

metrics.description: Server SQL mode (sql_mode). Must include STRICT_TRANS_TABLES to surface invalid values as errors instead of silent coercion.
metrics.remediation: Add STRICT_TRANS_TABLES,NO_ENGINE_SUBSTITUTION to sql_mode in my.cnf

metrics.description: Deprecated MySQL functions or syntax in stored routines. Must be cleaned up before upgrading to a major version that removes them.
metrics.remediation: Run MySQL upgrade checker: mysqlcheck --check-upgrade or mysqlsh util.checkForServerUpgrade()

metrics.description: User-data tables on the MyISAM engine. Must be migrated to InnoDB for crash recovery, row-level locking, and forward compatibility.
metrics.remediation: Convert MyISAM tables to InnoDB for crash recovery and row-level locking

metrics.description: Server/table character set. Must be utf8mb4; utf8mb3 is deprecated and cannot represent the full Unicode range (e.g. emoji).
metrics.remediation: Migrate tables from utf8mb3 to utf8mb4; set character_set_server = utf8mb4

metrics.description: Whether the instance is wired to a monitoring system (PMM, Zabbix, etc.). Required to detect issues before they cause downtime.
metrics.remediation: Connect MySQL to Percona Monitoring and Management (PMM) or Zabbix

metrics.description: Whether alerts exist for critical MySQL metrics (replication lag, connection saturation, disk usage). Required for incident response.
metrics.remediation: Configure alerts for replication lag, connection saturation, disk usage

metrics.description: Whether the slow query log is analysed regularly (pt-query-digest, MySQL Workbench, etc.). Required to surface and act on offending queries.
metrics.remediation: Use pt-query-digest or MySQL Workbench to analyze slow query log periodically

metrics.description: Whether schema and configuration changes follow a controlled change-management process. Required to catch regressions before they reach production.
metrics.remediation: Implement schema migration tooling (Liquibase, Flyway) and change approval process

metrics.description: Whether SSL/TLS support is compiled into the server (have_ssl). Without it, encrypted connections are not possible regardless of client config.
metrics.remediation: Ensure MySQL is compiled with SSL support and ssl-ca/ssl-cert/ssl-key are configured

metrics.description: Whether a server audit plugin (MariaDB Audit or MySQL Enterprise Audit) is loaded. Required for compliance audit trails.
metrics.remediation: Enable audit logging: INSTALL PLUGIN server_audit SONAME "server_audit" (MariaDB) or audit_log (MySQL Enterprise)

metrics.description: InnoDB buffer pool size (innodb_buffer_pool_size). Must be sized for the working set; rule of thumb is 70-80% of available RAM on dedicated servers.
metrics.remediation: Set innodb_buffer_pool_size to 70-80% of available RAM for dedicated database servers

metrics.description: Whether total database data size (DATA_LENGTH + INDEX_LENGTH) has been measured. Required as input to capacity planning.
metrics.remediation: Monitor total data size growth trends for capacity planning

metrics.description: Whether SELECT query throughput (Com_select) is being captured. Required as a baseline for trend and anomaly detection.
metrics.remediation: Enable Performance Schema and monitor Com_select counter for throughput trends
